title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 42
paragraphs: In the course of this year nothing further was done by the Persians that tended to strife with the Ionians; but the following things were done in this year very much to their advantage. Artaphrenes the governor of Sardis sent for envoys from all the cities and compelled the Ionians to make agreements among themselves, so that they would give satisfaction for wrongs and not plunder one another's land. This he compelled them to do; he also measured their territories in parasangs—this is the name the Persians give to thirty furlongs—and, measuring by these, he appointed a certain amount of tribute for each people, which continues unaltered even to my own day, just as Artaphrenes appointed it; the tribute was set at nearly the same amount for each as it had been before.
